claims.author: luke-jr
claims.harm: returning an array instead of an object prevents future extensibility of the listprunelocks RPC response
claims.quote: This was an Object for future extensibility. No reason to lose that.

status_by.quote: fair enough, I have changed it to return an object.

claims.status_note: author updated listprunelocks to return an object

claims.author: bvbfan
claims.quote: You could get it as copy and don't keep lock while iterating, performance wise.
claims.request: copy prune locks instead of holding cs_main lock while iterating

claims.author: sedited
claims.question: asks who mentioned the specific users or use cases for the feature
claims.quote: Do you remember at least who mentioned these users/use cases?

status_by.quote: This is generally useful in the wallet and for any wallets that leverage Bitcoin Core.

claims.status_note: achow101 detailed the wallet rescan use cases

claims.author: stickies-v
claims.quote: This looks potentially interesting, but I don't think we should be implementing RPCs when we don't know anyone that would actually be using them?
claims.request: questioned whether there is real demand or known users to justify adding the RPCs

status_by.quote: Thanks for the explanation @achow101 . Concept ACK.

claims.status_note: achow101 explained wallet rescanning on pruned nodes and stickies-v Concept ACKed

claims.author: stickies-v
claims.quote: I think this might be useful to include in PR description to give it more motivation?
claims.request: include the wallet rescan motivation in the PR description

status_by.quote: Done, replace that vague part of the description with a better motivation paragraph.

claims.author: sedited
claims.question: asks how prune locks are useful to external applications if they are not persisted across restarts
claims.quote: One thing that is still not clear to me is how this is actually useful to external applications if the locks are not persisted.
claims.status_note: author discussed and added the -prunelockheight startup option which reviewer agreed with and approved

claims.author: sedited
claims.harm: iterating over prune locks container without holding lock or copying risks data race
claims.quote: Don't we either have to hold this lock while iterating through the prune locks, or copy them? I think my preference would be to just take a copy here.
claims.status_note: author implemented explicit copy before lock scope ends; reviewer later approved

claims.author: sedited
claims.question: asks why a helper getter is introduced rather than iterating directly
claims.quote: Is there a reason for introducing this helper? Existing validation code that iterates through the locks directly.

status_by.quote: m_prune_locks is private and the direct access to it in validation.cpp is only possible because ChainState is a friend class of BlockManager.

claims.author: rkrux
claims.question: asks if the startup option can cause -prune to not be respected
claims.quote: Can't there be a case wherein this new argument causes the -prune=<n> option to not be respected?

status_by.quote: Yes, unless I am misunderstanding your question that is the whole idea behind prune locks

claims.status_note: author confirmed that is the intended behavior of prune locks and pointed to PR 21726

claims.author: rkrux
claims.quote: Also, a functional test for wallet exercising prune locks that solves the above scenario would be nice.
claims.request: add functional test for wallet exercising prune locks

status_by.quote: I added this in a separate commit. I folded it into the existing test file since generating all those blocks is pretty expensive

claims.status_note: author added a functional test covering wallet prune locks

claims.author: rkrux
claims.question: asks if INITIAL_BLOCKS in functional test can be halved
claims.quote: Is this correct? The following diff passes where this value is halved along with the corresponding heights in the pruneblockchain RPCs.

status_by.quote: for me the proposed diff fails because the blocks are not enough to get actual pruning.

claims.status_note: author noted the diff fails locally and kept the minimum reliable value

claims.author: rkrux
claims.quote: prune_height_locked is -1 because the lock prevents the pruning from happening. I don't see much point in asserting that prune_height_unlocked is greater than prune_height_locked.
claims.request: suggested improving test assertion since prune_height_locked is -1

status_by.quote: Changed this to check for -1 and >0 more explicitly now.

claims.status_note: author changed test to check explicitly for -1 and >0

claims.author: rkrux
claims.quote: The changes in this file require a release note because of new RPCs being added. Along with the new startup option.
claims.request: add release notes for the new RPCs and startup option

status_by.quote: Right, added the necessary release notes!

claims.author: rkrux
claims.question: asks whether allowing prune locks on future block heights is intentional
claims.quote: There isn't a check that forbids locking blocks that'd be generated in the future. Is it intentional?

status_by.quote: Right, that's a good observation, I didn't think about this explicitly so far but I don't see harm in allowing this and it may even be useful for some use-cases.

claims.status_note: author explained it can be useful and added a documentation note

claims.author: rkrux
claims.quote: Ok, can add a sentence here that this option will cause the -prune option to not be respected - just to be explicit.
claims.request: explicitly mention in init.cpp help that -prunelockheight causes -prune to not be respected
claims.status_note: author added the note to help text

claims.author: sedited
claims.quote: Maybe mention here that the lock may be viewed by `listprunelock`and removed by `setprunelock`.
claims.request: mention in release notes that the init lock can be viewed and removed by RPC

status_by.quote: I changed this and renamed the prefix to `user:` since it's not strictly used by RPCs anymore.

claims.status_note: author updated release notes and adjusted prefix to user: to allow removing it via RPC

claims.author: andrewtoth
claims.quote: I'm not sure I find the motivation compelling. Would the same functionality be achieved via the `pruneblockchain` RPC and a `-prune=1` setting?
claims.request: questioned whether manual prune locks are needed over using -prune=1 and pruneblockchain RPC

status_by.quote: Partly yes, but I think it would be much more complex and difficult to implement managing that behavior on the side of an external wallet.

claims.status_note: author explained that managing manual pruning from an external wallet requires reimplementing automatic pruning logic
